title: Source-first IA display contract
summary: This iteration added the repository contract needed to make subscribed sources and platform status a first-class public data surface. It defines fixed source display sections and ranks, extends source_effectiveness rows with display metadata and reader-facing status labels, keeps public docs data sanitized, and documents how future sources should be inserted into the fixed order.

lessons.lesson: Source visibility needs a stable display contract instead of being inferred from whichever source happened to produce a candidate today.
lessons.evidence: config/source-display-contract.json now assigns fixed sections, ranks, and default expansion modes to the public source-effectiveness surface.
lessons.recommended_action: Add future logical sources to the display contract at the same time as their collection contract, using rank gaps for later insertion.

lessons.lesson: Blocked and skipped source states should be public reader-facing statuses, not implicit absence.
lessons.evidence: source_effectiveness rows now emit status_label values including blocked and not_configured_or_skipped, and unit tests cover blocked precedence over parsed-but-not-candidate signals.
lessons.recommended_action: Use these labels directly in the next UI phase so outages and unconfigured sources are visible without exposing private audit details.

followups.action: Implement the first-screen story and source metrics dashboard using the new source_effectiveness display fields.
Render the fixed source graph with default expanded sections, collapsed long-tail sections, and visible blocked or skipped source rows.
